seo.title: Best Street Food in Antwerp (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover Antwerp's top street food spots, from iconic Belgian fries and waffles to gourmet global bites. Our 2026 guide features local favorites and hidden gems for every budget.

hero.subtitle: Antwerp's vibrant streets are a culinary playground, offering an irresistible mix of traditional Belgian delights and exciting international flavors perfect for on-the-go exploration.

picks.name: Frituur No. 1
picks.whyItMadeTheList: An Antwerp institution, Frituur No. 1 has been serving up crispy, golden Belgian fries from its prime location near the Grote Markt for decades. It's a no-frills spot where tradition reigns, known for its perfectly fried potatoes and wide array of classic sauces. The atmosphere is bustling and authentically Belgian, making it a must-visit.
picks.whatToOrder: Fries with Stoofvlees (Flemish beef stew) sauce, or a classic Andalouse sauce.
picks.insiderTip: Go during off-peak hours to avoid the longest queues, especially on weekends. Don't be shy to try a local sauce you've never heard of!
picks.redditQuote: "Frituur No. 1 is hands down the best for a classic Belgian friet. Nothing beats their stoofvlees sauce after a day exploring the Grote Markt."

picks.name: Bia Mara
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Bia Mara elevates the humble fish and chips to an art form, focusing on sustainable, lesser-known fish species and inventive coatings. While it offers seating, its quick service and takeaway option make it perfect for gourmet street food. Their commitment to fresh ingredients and creative flavor combinations sets them apart, offering a refined twist on a classic.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Classic Haddock & Chips' with their homemade tartare sauce, or try a rotating special like the panko-crusted pollock.
picks.insiderTip: They often have creative seasonal specials; check their board for unique fish varieties and spicy or unusual coatings.
picks.redditQuote: "If you want next-level fish and chips, Bia Mara is your spot. Way better than typical pub fare; the different fish options are always a win."

picks.name: Wafelhuis Van Hecke
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Serving traditional Belgian waffles since 1905, Wafelhuis Van Hecke is a historic gem for sweet tooths. They specialize in both Liège waffles (chewy, dense, with pearl sugar) and Brussels waffles (lighter, crispier, rectangular). Located centrally, it’s perfect for a quick, authentic sweet treat while exploring the city.
picks.whatToOrder: A warm Liège waffle, plain or with a drizzle of Belgian chocolate.
picks.insiderTip: For a truly authentic experience, try the Liège waffle plain or just with a dusting of powdered sugar to appreciate its true flavor.
picks.redditQuote: "Wafelhuis Van Hecke is my go-to for a proper Belgian waffle. So much better than the tourist traps; the Liège waffles are perfection."

picks.name: Frites Atelier (Sergio Herman)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: This isn't just a frituur; it's a culinary experience by Michelin-starred chef Sergio Herman. Frites Atelier takes Belgian fries to a gourmet level with meticulously sourced potatoes, double-frying, and unique, high-quality toppings like truffle mayo, Flemish beef stew, or Indonesian satay. The sleek, modern interior offers a fast-casual yet refined setting for enjoying superior fries.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Flemish Beef Stew' fries for a hearty, local flavor, or the 'Truffle Mayo' for a luxurious treat.
picks.insiderTip: Expect higher prices than a traditional frituur, but the quality and gourmet toppings are worth the splurge for a unique experience.
picks.redditQuote: "Frites Atelier changed my view on fries. Yeah, it's pricier, but Sergio Herman's truffle mayo is actual heaven on earth. Worth every Euro!"

picks.name: De Broodjeszaak
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A local favorite for fresh, generously filled sandwiches, De Broodjeszaak offers a taste of authentic Belgian lunch culture. They're known for their wide variety of fillings, from classic cheese and ham to more adventurous combinations, all served on freshly baked bread. It's a bustling spot popular with locals for a quick, satisfying and affordable meal.
picks.whatToOrder: A 'Broodje Martino' (raw minced meat, pickles, onion, tartare sauce) or a 'Broodje Krabsalade' (crab salad).
picks.insiderTip: Lines can be long during lunchtime, especially weekdays. If you're overwhelmed by choices, ask for a 'Dagsoep' (soup of the day) and a popular classic sandwich.
picks.redditQuote: "For a real Antwerp lunch experience, De Broodjeszaak is top-tier. Their broodjes are fresh, huge, and so cheap. Get the Martino if you're brave!"

picks.name: Falafel Tof
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Falafel Tof is a beloved vegetarian institution in Antwerp, renowned for its fresh, flavorful falafel. Everything is made in-house, from the crispy falafel balls to the tangy sauces and fluffy pita bread. The casual, vibrant atmosphere and consistent quality make it a go-to for a healthy and delicious street food option in the city center.
picks.whatToOrder: A classic Falafel sandwich, loaded with salad and your choice of sauces like tahini or spicy harissa.
picks.insiderTip: Don't skip the pickled turnip and other fresh vegetable toppings; they add essential crunch and tang to your falafel.
picks.redditQuote: "Seriously, Falafel Tof has the best falafel in Antwerp. It’s always fresh, perfectly crispy, and those sauces are just divine."

picks.name: Noodle Bar Lam & Yin
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Nestled in Antwerp's Chinatown, Noodle Bar Lam & Yin offers an authentic taste of Hong Kong-style street food, specializing in delicious noodle soups and roasted meats. The small, bustling eatery provides a genuine feel of Asian street food culture, with quick service and hearty portions that are perfect for a warming meal on the go. It’s a true local's spot.
picks.whatToOrder: The Wonton Noodle Soup or the Roast Duck Noodle Soup.
picks.insiderTip: This place is small and can get very busy; be prepared to share a table or grab your order to go and enjoy it in a nearby park.
picks.redditQuote: "Lam & Yin's wonton noodles are legit. Tastes just like what I had in Hong Kong. Best Asian street food vibe in Antwerp."

picks.name: Pakske friet
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A highly-rated modern frituur near the iconic Central Station, Pakske friet has quickly gained a reputation for its excellent fries and friendly service. They focus on quality potatoes, fresh oil, and a wide selection of sauces and snacks, making it a reliable spot for a quintessential Belgian fry experience without the deep historical context of some older establishments.
picks.whatToOrder: Fries with a 'Special' sauce (mayo, ketchup, chopped onion) or a 'Curryworst Speciaal'.
picks.insiderTip: Perfect for grabbing a quick bite before or after catching a train; it's conveniently located and consistently good.
picks.redditQuote: "Pakske friet around Central Station is my favorite spot. Their fries are always perfectly crispy, and the portions are generous. A reliable choice."

picks.name: Bubble Waffle Cafe
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Bringing a taste of Hong Kong to Antwerp, Bubble Waffle Cafe offers the unique, airy, and crispy 'egg' waffles, often filled with ice cream and various toppings. It's a fun, modern take on street food dessert, popular among younger crowds and those looking for an Instagrammable treat. The customizable options make every waffle a personal creation.
picks.whatToOrder: A bubble waffle with your choice of ice cream (e.g., speculoos or matcha) and fresh fruit or chocolate sauce.
picks.insiderTip: They have vegan options for both the waffle batter and ice cream, making it a great choice for those with dietary restrictions.
picks.redditQuote: "The bubble waffles at Bubble Waffle Cafe are so good and super photogenic! Definitely worth a stop for a sweet treat after shopping on the Meir."

picks.name: Frituur Piro
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Tucked away in the charming Sint-Andries district, Frituur Piro is a local gem known for its quality fries and extensive menu of 'frituur snacks.' It's a no-frills, authentic spot that consistently delivers perfectly fried potatoes and a warm, welcoming atmosphere. Popular with both locals and students, it's a great late-night stop.
picks.whatToOrder: A classic 'Bicky Burger' with fries and their famous 'mammouth' sauce.
picks.insiderTip: Piro is known for its generous portions, so consider ordering a 'small' or sharing if you're not extremely hungry.
picks.redditQuote: "Frituur Piro in Sint-Andries is peak local frituur. Always busy, always fresh, and their Bicky Burger is the real deal. Great for after-hours."

picks.name: Mevlana Döner & Kebab
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located on the bustling Brederodestraat, Mevlana Döner & Kebab is a cornerstone of Antwerp's Turkish culinary scene. This popular spot serves up hearty and flavorful döner and shoarma, often grilled to perfection and served in fresh pita bread or as a generous platter. It's a go-to for a quick, satisfying, and authentically spiced meal, especially after dark.
picks.whatToOrder: A classic 'Döner Kebab' in pita with all the fresh vegetables and a mix of garlic and spicy sauces.
picks.insiderTip: This area is bustling with various international eateries. Pair your kebab with a refreshing Ayran (Turkish yogurt drink) for a complete experience.
picks.redditQuote: "Mevlana has some of the best döner in Antwerp, especially after a few beers. Always fresh meat, huge portions, and the spicy sauce hits right."

picks.name: De Burgerij
picks.whyItMadeTheList: De Burgerij elevates the classic burger to a gourmet level, offering handcrafted patties with unique toppings and quality ingredients. While it has full sit-down restaurants, its focus on quick, quality burgers makes it a fantastic upscale street food option. They pride themselves on fresh, local produce and offer a range of creative burger combinations and excellent Belgian beers.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Chef's Burger' for a rotating special, or the 'Black Angus Burger' with a side of sweet potato fries.
picks.insiderTip: Though you can dine in, grabbing a burger to go and finding a nice spot in a nearby park like Harmoniepark (near the Zurenborg location) is a great street food experience.
picks.redditQuote: "If you're craving a really good, juicy burger, De Burgerij never disappoints. A bit more expensive but worth it for the quality. Pairs great with a Belgian beer."

faq.question: What is typical street food in Antwerp?
faq.answer: Antwerp's street food scene is rich with Belgian classics like crispy 'frietjes' (fries) served with a huge variety of sauces, and delicious 'wafels' (waffles) – both Liège and Brussels styles. Beyond these, you'll find hearty 'broodjes' (sandwiches), artisanal croquettes, and a growing presence of international flavors from Turkish kebabs to Asian noodles.

faq.question: Where are the best areas for street food in Antwerp?
faq.answer: The historic city center around Grote Markt and Groenplaats is a hub for traditional Belgian street food. For a more diverse range, explore the area around Central Station and the Meir for a mix of classic and modern options. Chinatown offers excellent Asian street eats, and districts like Sint-Andries and 't Zuid have great local fritkots and trendy spots.

faq.question: Is street food in Antwerp vegetarian-friendly?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Many street food venues in Antwerp offer excellent vegetarian options. Falafel Tof is a dedicated vegetarian spot, and most fritkots offer veggie burgers or cheese croquettes. You can also find vegetarian sandwiches, spring rolls, and increasingly, plant-based options at various international stalls and modern eateries.

faq.question: What makes Belgian fries unique?
faq.answer: Belgian fries, or 'frietjes,' are renowned worldwide for their distinct preparation. They are typically thick-cut, twice-fried in beef fat (traditionally, though vegetable oil is also common now), resulting in a crispy exterior and a fluffy interior. They're traditionally served in a paper cone with a small plastic fork and a generous dollop of mayonnaise or another classic Belgian sauce.

faq.question: How much does street food typically cost in Antwerp?
faq.answer: Street food in Antwerp is generally very affordable. A generous portion of fries will cost around €4-7 ($5-9), while a classic waffle is about €4-8 ($5-10). More elaborate sandwiches or international street food like kebabs and gourmet fries typically range from €8-15 ($10-18), offering great value for a satisfying meal.

faq.question: Is it safe to eat street food in Antwerp?
faq.answer: Yes, it is generally very safe to eat street food in Antwerp. Belgium has high food safety standards, and vendors are regularly inspected. Look for places with high foot traffic, which indicates freshness and popularity. Trust your instincts, but overall, you can enjoy the city's street food scene without concern.

methodology: Our selection of Antwerp's best street food spots is curated based on extensive local research, popular reviews, and personal visits. We prioritize authenticity, quality ingredients, and a diverse range of culinary experiences, ensuring a mix of traditional favorites and innovative newcomers for every palate and budget.
